deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (from the previous page). The instrument is a divided circle read by three micrometer microscopes: the lower one U near 0°, a left one L near 270° and a right one R near 90°. After bending the index and resetting the carrier of U, Gauss tightened the cords holding the microscopes. This page records a new series with the index on 0' and U set by its micrometer to 5'0".

1. RAW READINGS. The circle was set in 24 positions θ = 0°, 15°, ..., 345°. They are grouped in six sets of four positions 90° apart: {0,90,180,270}, {15,105,195,285}, ..., {75,165,255,345}. For each θ the seconds of L (beyond 270°0') and R (beyond 90°4') are recorded. R is written as 4'5x".

2. 'Abstände' (distances of L and R from U's 5' mark). For each set of four, Gauss takes the arithmetic mean of L and of R:
- L means: (9.1+10.2+11.3+9.7)/4 = 10.075 ≈ 10.08; 10.85; 10.625 ≈ 10.63; (11.5+11.9+8.5+10.4)/4 = 10.575 ≈ 10.58; 11.025 ≈ 11.02; 10.05.
- R means: 51.99, 52.05, 51.93, 51.88, 52.25, 51.73. The 30° and 45° sets only reproduce if the corrected digits are read as 52.8 and 52.1.
- Grand means: L = 63.21/6 = 10".535 → written 10"53. R = 311.83/6 = 51".97, written 4'51"96.
So with U at 5'0", the micrometer distance U→L is 10.53" and U→R is 4'51.96". Each value is averaged over 24 positions of the circle, so that division errors cancel.

3. PURPOSE. This series pairs with the next page (index at −5', R on 0). There Gauss concludes that the sum of the screw revolutions ('Inbegriff der Schraubengänge') of the lower microscope is 0".50 too small and that of R is 0".41 too large. The page is therefore a calibration of the micrometer screw value (the 'run') over a 5' interval.

4. 'Calc' TABLE.
- Column 1 gives, for each of the 24 positions (plus four later insertions at 50, 230, 140, 320), a small quantity whose sum within each set of four is zero. Examples: −0.88−0.14+1.11−0.09 = 0 and −0.46−0.04+1.24−0.74 = 0. The 15° set sums to 0.29, presumably a slip. These are evidently the reduced periodic deviations per position, defined only up to a constant within each set of four.
- I could not reproduce column 1 exactly from the raw readings by any simple combination: group deviations of L, of R, of (L+R)/2, of L−R, or the closed-cycle least-squares solution for division errors with L and R diametrically opposite. Its exact derivation is uncertain.
- Column 2 is the fitted formula ('Formel') c(x) = −0".79 cos x + 0".03 sin x, tabulated at 15° steps. All tabulated values check, e.g. x = 15: −0.763+0.008 = −0.755 → −0.76; x = 75: −0.204+0.029 = −0.175 → −0.18; second half antisymmetric.
- [Mine] A least-squares first-harmonic fit to column 1 (a = (1/12)Σ c cos x, b = (1/12)Σ c sin x over 24 points) gives a ≈ −0.72 and b ≈ +0.024. This agrees well with b and roughly with a. Gauss's a = −0.79 may use additional or revised data, e.g. the inserted positions 50/230/140/320.

5. 'Mittlerer Ablesungsfehler' (mean reading error): √0.84275 = 0".918, arithmetically correct. The origin of the variance 0.84275 is not shown. It is not Σ(col1−col2)²/24, which is ≈ 0.142. It is presumably a sum of squared deviations of single readings divided by the degrees of freedom.
errors: The 15° set of column 1 sums to +0.29 instead of 0 (−0.27−0.03+0.75−0.16); probably a slip or misread digit.
The R grand mean computes to 51".97 (311.83/6, or 1247.25/24 = 51.969); Gauss wrote 51"96, a trivial rounding difference.

The coefficient −0.79 in the formula is somewhat larger in magnitude than a straightforward least-squares harmonic fit to column 1 as written (≈ −0.72). The sine coefficient (0.03 vs 0.024) agrees. The basis of the fit is not fully shown.
The derivation of column 1 and of the variance 0.84275 is not written out on the page; they cannot be verified from the page alone.

results.what: Determination of the micrometer value (run) of the microscopes over 5', by reading L and R against U set at 5'0" in 24 circle positions and averaging per group of four.
results.modern_name: Run-of-micrometer calibration / elimination of division errors by rotating the circle
results.usually_credited_to: Standard practice of 19th-century meridian-circle astronomy (Bessel, Reichenbach/Repsold instruments)

results.what: Fitting the periodic error −0.79 cos x + 0.03 sin x to the 24 residuals.
results.modern_name: Least-squares fit of a first Fourier harmonic (trigonometric interpolation / harmonic analysis of eccentricity-type error)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Bessel (least squares, trigonometric interpolation c. 1805–1820)

results.what: Mean reading error as the square root of an average squared deviation: √0.84275 = 0.918".

deep.surprise_reason: Routine instrumental calibration in an observing journal: microscope-run determination, harmonic fit of a periodic error, and a mean error. All of these are well-known parts of Gauss's and Bessel's practice.

checkable.asserts: Mean of L in the 0° set = 10.075 ≈ 10.08 (implies the first Abstände entry is 10.08, not 10.98)
45° set L mean = 10.575 if the third reading is 8.5
30° set R mean = 51.925 if the last reading is 52.8
Column 1 sums to zero over the 0/90/180/270 set
Column 1 for the 15° set sums to 0.29, not 0 (probable slip)

transcription_corrections: Abstände, first L entry: read 10"08, not 10"98 (required by the readings 9.1, 10.2, 11.3, 9.7 and by the mean 10"53).
45° set, third L reading: 8.5 (overwritten), not 8.8; this gives the group mean 10.58.
30° set, last R reading (overwritten): evidently 52.8 rather than 52.2, to give the mean 51.93.
45° set, third R reading (overwritten): evidently 52.1 rather than 52.4, to give the mean 51.88.
The small entries at 50 (−1.50), 140 (−0.25), 230 (+1.26) and 320 (+0.49) are later interlinear insertions, not part of the regular 15° sequence.
